pairs.why: Real kit is seen in a mild three-quarter turn with the bass drum angled and the platform seen slightly from above, which B matches, while A is a flat, symmetric front-on elevation.
Real is a close, fairly high view with the dock filling the frame and a shallow background, and B is nearer and more top-down than A's distant wide shot with a far horizon.
Real has a nearly horizontal truss across the top with the lamp hanging below at mild perspective, which A matches, while B tilts the truss steeply with stronger perspective.
Real shows a high diagonal view with a lot of top face and no horizon, and A shows more top surface with a plain backdrop, while B is lower, more frontal and has a visible wall/table horizon line.
Both put a simple hedge behind the hero and use a similar camera height; A's base ellipse and path wrap sit slightly closer to the real shallow ground angle, but the difference is marginal.
Both show the same high, mild three-quarter top view of two sandals on a flat striped backdrop, so there is no viewpoint difference to separate them.
A's ball is a little closer and shows the top cap from slightly above, like the real ball, though both add a dune horizon the real card doesn't have.
B's floorboards converge less and the camera is a little lower, nearer the real card's mild perspective, whereas A's boards fan out in a wider-angle way.
